measurements.evidence_quote: The zeta potentials of these nanoplastics were -11.5 ± 1.48 mV (N = 6 measurements) (see more detailed properties of YG polystyrene nanoplastics in Section ). || The electrical charge of the surfaces of nanoplastic particles in a suspension, which means the zeta potential, was measured via a zeta potential analyzer, ZetaPlus (Brookhaven Instruments), located in the Materials, Design and Manufacturing Facility of HKUST. || Prior to the measurement, nanoplastics were dissolved in deionized water and diluted to 10 μg/mL, followed by vortexing for 30 s to make nanoparticles spread evenly in a suspension and to minimize the aggregation and flocculation of the particles. || Measurements were taken at room temperature, and 10 runs per measurement were conducted.
